title: Manitoba RCMP officer won't face charges for fatal 2011 First Nation shooting
subtitle: An RCMP officer who shot an armed man in Manitoba's God's Lake First Nation last March will not face charges
article: An RCMP officer who shot an armed man in Manitoba's God's Lake First Nation last March will not face charges.
The Saskatoon Police Service announced Wednesday morning they'd completed their investigation into the March 2011 shooting.
The shooting occurred while two officers from the God's Lake Narrows RCMP were guarding the scene of a house fire.
They were confronted by an armed man, 52-year-old Paul Leonard Duck.
One officer fired at Duck and hit him twice. Duck was declared dead at the local nursing station.
The incident was also reviewed by Crown counsel in Ontario, which found "no evidence to support criminal charges."
There will still be an inquest looking into the circumstances around Duck's death.
